examples.en: The wizard in the story uses magic.
Children like magic stories.
The problem was solved like magic.
Shall we recite a magic spell?

examples.ko: 눈이 오자 마을은 마법에 걸린 것 같았어요.
examples.en: When snow fell, the town looked as if under a spell.

examples.ko: 저는 어렸을 때 마법사가 되고 싶었어요.
examples.en: When I was little I wanted to be a wizard.

explain: '마법'은 이야기 속의 힘을 말해요. 손으로 하는 '마술'은 사람이 보여 주는 기술이라 달라요. '마법사', '마법의 힘'처럼 말하고 비유로 놀랍게 잘 풀린 일에도 써요.

phrases.en: Yesterday was truly a magical day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 놀랍게 좋은 일을 비유로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used figuratively for wonderfully good things.

phrases.en: The princess was put under a spell.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이야기 속에서 자주 나오는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase often seen in stories.

phrases.en: This ring has magical power.
phrases.nuance_ko: '~의'로 이어서 힘이나 물건을 꾸며요.
phrases.nuance_en: Linked with '~의' to describe a power or object.

explain_en: 마법 is the power found in stories. 마술 is a performed trick done by a person, so they differ. You say 마법사 (wizard) or 마법의 힘 (magic power), and the word is also used figuratively for something that worked out amazingly well.

examples.en: At the wedding, the bride threw the bouquet.
The bouquet was made beautifully with white roses.
The bouquet the bride is holding is really pretty.
I heard the groom picked out the bouquet himself too.
I tied a small ribbon on the bouquet.

examples.ko: 부케 던지기 행사를 할 때 모두 웃었어요.
examples.en: Everyone laughed during the bouquet toss.

explain: '꽃다발'은 모든 꽃 묶음을 가리키고, '부케'는 주로 결혼식에서 신부가 드는 꽃다발에 써요. '부케를 던지다', '부케를 받다'처럼 써요. 부케를 받은 사람이 다음에 결혼한다는 말이 있어요.

phrases.en: I caught the bouquet at my friend's wedding.
phrases.nuance_ko: '부케를 던지다'와 짝이 되는 말로, 결혼식에서 부케를 받는 사람에게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The counterpart of 'throwing the bouquet'; used for the person who catches it at a wedding.

phrases.en: The bride's bouquet is really pretty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누구의 부케인지 밝힐 때 '신부'를 앞에 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put 'bride' in front to say whose bouquet it is.

phrases.en: I received a bunch of flowers at my graduation.
phrases.nuance_ko: '부케'보다 넓은 말로, 모든 꽃 묶음에 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A broader word than 'bouquet'; it works for any bunch of flowers.

explain_en: '꽃다발' covers any bunch of flowers, while '부케' is mainly the bunch a bride holds at a wedding. Say '부케를 던지다' (throw) and '부케를 받다' (catch). There is a saying that whoever catches it will marry next.

examples.en: In college I joined a photography club.
Our club meets every Friday.
I married a friend I met in the club.
A new club started at the school.
I'm thinking about which club to choose.
The film club is accepting new members too.

explain: 같은 취미로 모인 학생이나 젊은 사람들의 모임을 가리켜요. 요즘은 학교 모임을 '동아리', 취미 모임을 '동호회'라고 더 많이 말해서 '서클'은 조금 옛날 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.en: I'm in a photography club at school.
phrases.nuance_ko: '서클'과 같은 뜻이고, 요즘은 '동아리'를 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 서클, but 동아리 is used more these days.

phrases.en: I joined the club following my friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모임에 새로 가입할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing for newly joining a group.

phrases.en: I went on a trip with my club friends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 모임에서 만난 친구를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for friends you met in the same club.

explain_en: It refers to a group of students or young people gathered around a shared hobby. Today people more often say 동아리 for a school group and 동호회 for a hobby group, so 서클 feels a bit dated.

examples.en: Baseball is usually played for nine innings.
Today's game ended after seven innings.

examples.ko: 우리 팀이 마지막 이닝에 두 점을 냈어요.
examples.en: Our team scored two runs in the last inning.
The pitcher shut down the first inning cleanly.
One inning took longer than I expected.

examples.ko: 저는 한 이닝도 못 보고 집에 갔어요.
examples.en: I went home without watching even one inning.

explain: '3회 초'처럼 '회'를 쓰기도 하고, '세 이닝'처럼 세는 말로도 써요. 한 이닝은 앞 반(초)과 뒤 반(말)으로 나뉘어요.

phrases.en: Our team scored in the top of the third inning.
phrases.nuance_ko: '이닝' 대신 '회'를 쓰고, '초'는 앞 반을 뜻해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses 회 instead of 이닝, and 초 means the first half.

phrases.en: Many runs were scored in the last inning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 경기의 끝 부분을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the final part of a game.

phrases.en: The inning ended, so the players go in to rest.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 이닝의 공격과 수비가 모두 끝났다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means both batting and fielding for that inning are done.

explain_en: You can also say '3회 초' using '회', or count with '세 이닝'. One inning is split into a top half (초) and a bottom half (말).

examples.en: Who is the composer of this song?
The composer played it himself on the piano.

examples.ko: 저는 유명한 작곡자를 만나서 사인을 받았어요.
examples.en: I met a famous composer and got an autograph.
The composer and the lyricist are the same person.

examples.ko: 작곡자 이름이 앨범 뒷면에 적혀 있어요.
examples.en: The composer's name is written on the back of the album.
I asked the composer for a song, but there's no reply.

explain: '작곡가'와 거의 같은데, 직업을 말할 때는 '작곡가'가 더 자연스러워요. 곡을 만든 사람 한 명을 가리킬 때 '작곡자'를 써요. 가사를 쓴 사람은 '작사가/작사자'예요.

phrases.example: 이 노래는 작곡자와 작사자가 같은 사람이에요.
phrases.en: The composer and the lyricist of this song are the same person.
phrases.nuance_ko: 곡을 만든 사람과 가사를 쓴 사람을 함께 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to talk about the person who made the music and the one who wrote the lyrics together.

phrases.en: He is a famous composer.
phrases.nuance_ko: '작곡자'와 뜻이 같지만 직업을 말할 때는 '작곡가'가 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means the same as '작곡자', but '작곡가' sounds more natural when you talk about a job.

phrases.en: I want to know who the composer of this piece is.
phrases.nuance_ko: 특정한 곡을 만든 사람 한 명을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to point to the one person who made a particular piece.

explain_en: It is almost the same as '작곡가', but for a profession '작곡가' sounds more natural. '작곡자' points to the person who made a particular piece. The person who wrote the lyrics is '작사가' or '작사자'.

examples.en: A raccoon dog came out on the mountain path last night.
Raccoon dogs mostly move around at night.
I smiled at the raccoon dog in the photo.
Please don't feed the raccoon dogs.
Raccoon dogs also live in Korean mountains.
I think the raccoon dog's face is cute.

explain: 한국의 '너구리'는 영어로 raccoon dog이고, 북미의 raccoon은 '라쿤'이라고 불러요. 그래서 둘은 서로 다른 동물이에요.

phrases.en: I saw one raccoon dog in the forest.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동물은 '마리'로 세요.
phrases.nuance_en: Animals are counted with 'mari'.

phrases.en: Wild raccoon dogs avoid people.
phrases.nuance_ko: 산이나 숲에 사는 너구리를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to raccoon dogs living in mountains or forests.

phrases.en: A raccoon is different from a raccoon dog.
phrases.nuance_ko: 북미에 사는 다른 동물이라 헷갈리지 않게 구분해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A different animal from North America, so keep them apart.

explain_en: The Korean '너구리' is the raccoon dog in English, while the North American raccoon is called '라쿤'. They are different animals.

examples.en: There are many old books and toys in the attic room.
Our attic room is narrow but very cozy.
My grandmother's house in the countryside has an attic room.
The stairs going up to the attic room are very steep.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날 아이들이 다락방에서 숨바꼭질을 해요.
examples.en: On rainy days the kids play hide-and-seek in the attic room.

examples.ko: 저는 다락방에 누워서 만화책을 읽는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: I like lying in the attic room and reading comic books.

explain: '다락'은 지붕 아래 짐을 두는 공간이고, 그곳에 이불이나 책상을 두고 방처럼 쓰면 다락방이라고 해요. 요즘 아파트에는 거의 없어서 옛날 집이나 동화·드라마에서 자주 만나요. [다락빵]으로 읽어요.

phrases.en: I put the blankets in the attic.
phrases.nuance_ko: 짐을 두는 공간을 말하고, 방처럼 쓰면 '다락방'이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The storage space itself; it becomes 다락방 when used like a room.

phrases.en: I climb up to the attic room by ladder.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다락방은 위에 있어서 '올라가다'와 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Because it is up high, it is often paired with 올라가다.
phrases.en_equiv: go up to the attic room

phrases.en: I can see stars from the attic window.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지붕 아래 방의 창문을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the window of the room under the roof.

explain_en: '다락' is the storage space under the roof; when people put bedding or a desk there and use it like a room, it becomes a 다락방. Modern apartments rarely have one, so you meet it in old houses, fairy tales, and dramas. It is read [다락빵].

examples.en: Rabbits have long hind legs, so they jump well.

examples.ko: 강아지가 뒷다리로 서서 간식을 달라고 했어요.
examples.en: The puppy stood on its hind legs and asked for a snack.
The back legs of the chair are weak, so you must be careful.
The cat hurt its hind leg and went to the animal hospital.

examples.ko: 말은 뒷다리에 힘을 주고 높이 뛰어올랐어요.
examples.en: The horse put strength into its hind legs and jumped high.
It is an animal whose front legs and hind legs are both strong.

explain: 반대는 '앞다리'예요. 다리가 네 개인 동물에 쓰고, 의자나 책상 같은 물건의 뒤쪽 다리에도 써요. 사람의 다리는 '앞'과 '뒤'로 나누지 않고 그냥 '다리'라고 해요.

phrases.en: The dog's front and back legs are both short.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒷다리의 반대말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 뒷다리.

phrases.en: The back leg of the chair broke.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건의 뒤쪽 다리를 말할 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also used for the back leg of an object.

phrases.en: The cat hurt its hind leg.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동물이 다친 곳을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this to say where an animal is hurt.

explain_en: The opposite is '앞다리'. It is used for four-legged animals, and also for the back legs of things like chairs or desks. A person's legs are not split into front and back; they are just '다리'.

en: to confront; to face each other

examples.ko: 두 사람이 책상을 사이에 두고 마주해서 이야기했어요.
examples.en: The two talked face to face with a desk between them.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 어려운 현실을 마주하고 있어요.
examples.en: He is facing a difficult reality.
It was an evening spent face to face with my family after a long time.

examples.ko: 문제를 피하지 말고 한번 마주해 보세요.
examples.en: Don't avoid the problem; try facing it.
When I opened the door, I came face to face with a stranger.

examples.ko: 두 사람은 마주하면 말없이 웃기만 해요.
examples.en: When the two come face to face, they just smile without a word.

explain: '만나다'는 약속하고 보는 것이고, '마주하다'는 얼굴이나 상황을 정면으로 대하는 느낌이에요. 사람뿐 아니라 '현실을 마주하다', '문제를 마주하다'처럼 피하고 싶은 일에도 써요. '마주 앉다', '마주 보다'는 띄어 쓰는 말이에요.

phrases.en: We sat facing each other at the table.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서로 얼굴을 보고 앉는다는 뜻이에요. 띄어 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means sitting face to face. Write it with a space.

phrases.en: The two people looked at each other and laughed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서로 정면으로 보는 모습이에요. 띄어 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It describes looking straight at each other. Write it with a space.

phrases.en: Now we have to face the problem.
phrases.nuance_ko: 피하고 싶은 일을 정면으로 대한다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It carries the feeling of facing something you would rather avoid.

explain_en: '만나다' is meeting by arrangement, while '마주하다' has the feel of facing a person or situation head-on. It is used not only for people but also for things you would rather avoid, as in '현실을 마주하다' (face reality). '마주 앉다' and '마주 보다' are written with a space.

examples.ko: 아이가 망토를 두르고 영웅 놀이를 해요.
examples.en: The child wears a cape and plays hero.
The cape fluttered in the wind.
In winter, a single cloak keeps me warm.
The black cloak has a hood attached.
You wear a cape draped over your shoulders.
I dressed up in a red cape.

explain: '빨간 망토'는 동화 제목으로도 유명해요. 겨울 외투는 보통 '코트'나 '외투'라고 하고, 망토는 만화나 옷 입기 놀이에 많이 나와요.

phrases.en: It was cold, so I put on a cape and went out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어깨 위에 가볍게 올려 입는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gives the feel of draping it loosely over the shoulders.

phrases.en: I read the story of 'Little Red Riding Hood' as a child.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동화 제목으로 자주 들어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often heard as the title of the fairy tale.

phrases.en: I came home and took off my cape.
phrases.nuance_ko: 입는 동작의 반대로, 벗을 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of putting it on; used for taking it off.

explain_en: 'Ppalgan mangto' (Little Red Riding Hood) is a famous fairy-tale title. A winter outer garment is usually a 'coat' or 'oetu'; mangto shows up in comics and dress-up play.

examples.ko: 황사 때문에 방금 세차한 차가 금방 먼지투성이가 됐어요.
examples.en: Because of the yellow dust, my freshly washed car quickly got covered in dust.
The room that has been empty for a long time is covered in dust.
I wiped the dusty bookshelf clean.
The child came home covered in dust.
The storeroom is dusty all over, so it needs cleaning.
Don't touch your face with dusty hands.

explain: '-투성이'는 흙투성이, 땀투성이, 상처투성이처럼 안 좋은 것이 온통 묻거나 가득할 때 붙여요. 보통 좋은 뜻의 말에는 쓰지 않아요. '먼지투성이가 되다', '먼지투성이다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: My clothes got covered in dust while cleaning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원래 깨끗했던 것이 먼지로 덮였을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when something that was clean gets covered in dust.

phrases.en: I wiped the dusty desk clean.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-인'을 붙여 뒤에 오는 명사를 꾸며요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-인' lets it describe the noun that follows.

phrases.en: There is too much dust in the storage room.
phrases.nuance_ko: '먼지투성이'보다 가볍고 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A lighter and simpler way to say it than '먼지투성이'.

explain_en: The suffix '-투성이' attaches to something unpleasant that covers or fills a thing, as in 흙투성이, 땀투성이 and 상처투성이. It is not normally used with positive things. You use it as in '먼지투성이가 되다' and '먼지투성이다'.
